name: Birmingham Roller
fact: Bred to somersault backwards in the air, sometimes many times in a row, then fly on as if nothing happened.

name: Western European house mouse
fact: Male mice sing ultrasonic courtship songs, too high-pitched for humans to hear.

name: Indian Runner duck
fact: Runs instead of waddling - farmers once walked whole flocks out to the rice paddies to eat pests.

name: Bubble Eye goldfish
fact: Its giant eye bubbles jiggle as it swims, and can pop - then slowly grow back.
credit: Angie Torres from Toronto · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Giant Canada goose
fact: Was thought extinct until a flock was found wintering in a city park in Minnesota.

name: Fancy rat
fact: Laughs (ultrasonically) when tickled, and will chase the hand that does it for more.

name: Polish chicken
fact: Its crest sprouts from a bony dome on its skull and can cover its eyes so much that it startles easily.

name: Common pill woodlouse
fact: Not an insect at all - it's a land crustacean, more closely related to shrimp.

name: Seven-spot ladybird
fact: Oozes bitter, smelly 'reflex blood' from its knees when threatened.
credit: Photographer: Dominik Stodulski Graphic Processing: User:MathKnight · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Canadian nightcrawler
fact: Breathes through its skin, which is why it surfaces when the ground floods.

name: Common housefly
fact: Tastes with its feet.

name: Sebastopol goose
fact: Its feathers curl so much that it looks permanently caught in a gale.

name: English Pouter
fact: Puffs its crop up until it looks like it swallowed a balloon.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
fact: Was bred to herd cattle by nipping their heels - the short legs keep it under the kicks.

name: Nine-banded armadillo
blurb: Species of armadillo native to South America
fact: Almost always gives birth to four identical clones from a single egg.

name: Flemish Giant rabbit
fact: One of the biggest rabbit breeds - some outweigh a small dog.

name: Blobfish
fact: Only looks like a blob out of water - at depth, it looks like a normal fish.

name: Lord Howe Island stick insect
fact: The 'tree lobster' was found again living under a single bush on Ball's Pyramid.

name: Olm
fact: A blind cave salamander that can go a decade without eating.

name: Pink fairy armadillo
fact: The smallest armadillo - pink because blood shows through its shell.

name: Purple frog
fact: Lives buried in the soil of India's Western Ghats and surfaces only for a couple of monsoon weeks to breed - it looks like a deflated purple blob with a pig snout.
credit: Original uploader was Karthickbala at ta.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Eastern cottontail
blurb: Species of rabbit in the genus Sylvilagus
fact: Escapes predators by running in sharp zigzags.

name: Brown garden snail
fact: Can seal itself inside its shell and sleep through months of drought.

name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
fact: Doubles its body weight in fat before crossing the Gulf of Mexico in one go.

name: North American beaver
fact: Its biggest known dam, in Canada's Wood Buffalo park, can be seen from space.
credit: Steve from Washington, DC, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Eastern spotted skunk
fact: Does a full handstand and walks on its front paws at you before spraying.
credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Midwest Region · Public domain

name: European hedgehog
fact: Chews toxic things and lathers the foamy spit onto its spines - nobody's sure why.

name: Florida box turtle
fact: A hinged shell lets it close up completely - a true box.

name: Mexican free-tailed bat
blurb: Species of bat native to the Americas
fact: Clocked at 160 km/h in level flight - possibly the fastest flier outside a dive.

name: Veiled chameleon
fact: Its tongue shoots out from 0 to 97 km/h in a hundredth of a second.

name: Atlantic puffin
fact: Its rough tongue pins fish against spines in its beak, so it can keep catching with a full mouth.

name: Blue-footed booby
fact: Males strut and lift their bright blue feet one at a time to impress females.

name: Black-tailed prairie dog
fact: Its alarm calls encode a predator's species, size, colour and speed.

name: Pygmy hippopotamus
fact: Moo Deng, a baby pygmy hippo in Thailand, became one of the most famous animals online in 2024.

name: Vaquita
fact: The rarest marine mammal on Earth.

name: Yeti crab
fact: The 'yeti crab' farms bacteria on its hairy arms - and may eat them.
credit: Andrew Thurber, Oregon State University · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Dumbo octopus
fact: The deepest-living octopus - it flaps its ear-like fins to 'fly' through the abyss.

name: Superb lyrebird
fact: Copies almost any sound - other birds, car alarms, chainsaws - perfectly.

name: Peacock spider
fact: The peacock spider - a male raises a jewel-coloured fan and dances to win a mate.

name: Immortal jellyfish
blurb: Species of small, biologically immortal jellyfish
fact: The 'immortal jellyfish' can turn back into a juvenile and start its life over.

name: Narwhal
fact: Its 'horn' is a tooth growing out through its lip, packed with millions of nerve endings.

name: Pistol shrimp
blurb: Family of crustacean possessing asymmetrical snapping claws
fact: Its claw snap fires a bubble that briefly gets nearly as hot as the surface of the sun.

name: Saiga antelope
fact: That bulbous nose is a built-in air filter for dusty summers and frozen winters.

name: Shoebill
fact: Looks like a dinosaur, eats lungfish and baby crocodiles, and 'claps' its bill to communicate.

name: West Indian Ocean coelacanth
fact: Thought extinct for 66 million years, until one turned up in a fishing net in 1938.

name: Pug
fact: Bred as lapdogs for Chinese emperors - some were kept in palaces with their own guards.

name: Dachshund
fact: Its loud bark is deliberate - so hunters could hear it underground.

name: Shetland pony
fact: Pound for pound one of the strongest horse breeds - it once hauled coal down mines.

name: Jacob sheep
fact: Rams can grow four or even six horns at once, sticking out in all directions.
credit: David Merrett from Daventry, England · CC BY 2.0

name: Silkie
blurb: Topics referred to by the same term
fact: Marco Polo described a "chicken with fur" - its fluffy feathers have no hooks to zip them flat.

name: Angora rabbit
fact: Its wool is warmer than sheep wool and is gathered by brushing or plucking as it moults.

name: Fainting goat
fact: When startled its muscles lock up and it often tips over - it doesn't actually faint.

name: Alpaca
blurb: Domesticated species of South American camelid
fact: A whole herd uses a few communal dung piles, which makes them easy to house-train.

name: Guinea pig
fact: Not a pig and not from Guinea - excited ones leap straight up in the air, called 'popcorning'.

name: Roborovski dwarf hamster
fact: The smallest hamster species, and one of the fastest for its size.

name: European herring gull
fact: Pecks the red spot on its parent's beak to make it cough up dinner.

name: Banana slug
fact: The second-largest land slug on Earth - its slime numbs the tongues of would-be predators.
credit: Andy.goryachev at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Monarch butterfly
blurb: Milkweed butterfly in the family Nymphalidae
fact: No single butterfly makes the round trip - it takes several generations to get back north.
credit: Photo by and (c)2007 Derek Ramsey (Ram-Man) · GFDL 1.2

name: Common earwig
fact: Despite the myth, it doesn't crawl into ears - but mothers do guard and clean their eggs.

name: Long-bodied cellar spider
fact: Shakes its web so fast it becomes a blur - and happily hunts other spiders.

name: Zebrafish
fact: Can regrow up to a fifth of its heart - which is why scientists study it so closely.

name: Siamese fighting fish
blurb: Species of fish native to Southeast Asia
fact: Males build floating nests of spit bubbles and guard the eggs inside.

name: Brine shrimp (Sea-Monkey)
fact: Their dried eggs can survive years of drought - and even a trip to space - then hatch in water.

name: Cane toad
fact: Brought to Australia to eat beetles; it ignored them and spread across the continent instead.

name: American bullfrog
fact: Eats almost anything it can fit in its mouth - including other bullfrogs, snakes and bats.

name: Common snapping turtle
fact: Can whip its head around astonishingly fast - and can reach back to its own hind legs.
credit: Chuck Homler, Focus On Wildlife · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Red-eared slider
fact: Named for the way it slides off rocks and logs into the water at the first sign of trouble.

name: Leopard gecko
fact: Unlike most geckos it has eyelids and can't climb glass - and blinks at you.

name: Central bearded dragon
fact: Waves one arm in a slow circle to signal submission to bigger dragons.
credit: Photograph: Frank C. Müller, Baden-Baden · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: Anolis carolinensis
fact: Often called the 'American chameleon' - it shifts between green and brown.

name: Eastern chipmunk
fact: Can gather up to 165 acorns a day, stuffing its cheeks to carry them home.

name: Wild turkey
blurb: Species of turkey native to North America
fact: Unlike farm turkeys, wild ones fly well and roost in trees at night.

name: Muscovy duck
fact: It hardly quacks at all - males hiss, and females make a small trilling coo.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Llama
fact: Some farmers use llamas as guards - they chase off foxes and coyotes from sheep flocks.

name: Baudet du Poitou
fact: Its shaggy coat grows into long cords called cadenettes - a status symbol in old France.

name: Mangalica
fact: A pig with a woolly fleece like a sheep - it nearly died out in the 1990s.

name: Kunekune
fact: Small enough to be a pet and grazes on grass, which most pigs cannot live on alone.

name: Belted Galloway
fact: Black at both ends with a white belt round the middle, just like a sandwich biscuit.

name: Valais Blacknose
fact: Black face, black knees and spiralling horns, with a white fleece that looks like a soft toy.

name: Lionhead rabbit
fact: A single dominant gene gives it a woolly mane around its head like a tiny lion.

name: Scottish Fold
blurb: Cat breed having specific gene mutation
fact: All Scottish Folds trace back to one barn cat named Susie - and many sit up 'Buddha style'.

name: Sphynx cat
fact: Not truly hairless - it has a fine down and feels like suede to stroke.

name: Basset Hound
fact: Its long ears drag along the ground to waft smells up toward its nose.

name: Komondor
fact: Its corded coat makes it look like a giant mop - and blend in with the flock it guards.
credit: Nikki68 at Russian Wikipedia · CC BY 2.5

name: Chinese Crested Dog
fact: Has won the World's Ugliest Dog Contest many times - it was once a sailor's ratter.

name: Xoloitzcuintle
fact: The Aztecs believed this hairless dog guided the dead through the underworld.
credit: Svenska Mässan from Sweden · CC BY 2.0

name: Puli dog
fact: Its coat naturally twists into cords - the dog underneath is surprisingly small.
credit: Original uploader was Elf at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Greyhound
fact: The fastest dog breed - but famously lazy, sleeping up to 18 hours a day.

name: Budgerigar
fact: A budgie named Puck held the world record for the biggest vocabulary of any bird.

name: Sulphur-crested cockatoo
fact: A cockatoo named Snowball could dance to the beat - wild ones teach each other to open bins.

name: Moon jellyfish
fact: Has no brain, heart or bones - and its sting is too weak for most people to feel.

name: Common starfish
fact: Pushes its stomach out of its mouth to digest a mussel inside its own shell.

name: Purple sea urchin
fact: Its five-toothed jaw is called Aristotle's lantern, after his description of it.
credit: Ed Bierman from CA, usa · CC BY 2.0

name: Caribbean hermit crab
fact: Lines up with others by size to swap shells in a chain when a new one turns up.

name: American lobster
blurb: Lobster of the western North Atlantic
fact: Chews with teeth inside its stomach and tastes with its legs.
credit: OAR/National Undersea Research Program (NURP). · Public domain

name: Hummingbird hawk-moth
fact: Hovers at flowers sipping nectar so convincingly that people report seeing hummingbirds in Europe.

name: Dryocampa rubicunda
fact: Looks like it was dyed for a birthday party - adults barely eat during their short lives.

name: Common eastern firefly
fact: Males draw a J-shaped flash in the air to court females, who flash back from the grass.
credit: art farmer from evansville indiana, usa · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Giant African land snail
fact: One of the most invasive species on Earth - it eats over 500 kinds of plant.

name: Attacus atlas
fact: Adults have no mouth and live only about a week - the wing tips mimic cobra heads.

name: Psittacosaurus
fact: One of the best-known dinosaurs - a fossil even preserved its skin colour: dark back, pale belly.

name: Protoceratops
fact: Found locked in combat with a Velociraptor, both buried mid-fight by a collapsing dune.
credit: Tadek Kurpaski from London, Poland · CC BY 2.0

name: Compsognathus
fact: Chicken-sized - one fossil was found with a whole lizard still in its stomach.
credit: Zach Tirrell from Plymouth, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Nigersaurus
fact: Its wide, straight-edged mouth mowed plants at ground level like a lawnmower.

name: Quokka
fact: Its upturned mouth makes it look like it is always smiling - selfies with it are a tourist rite.

name: Common wombat
fact: Produces cube-shaped poop and stacks it on rocks to mark its territory.

name: Tasmanian devil
fact: Has one of the strongest bites of any mammal for its size - it eats bones, fur and all.

name: Sugar glider
fact: Glides between trees on a skin membrane stretched from wrist to ankle.

name: Naked mole-rat
fact: Lives in colonies with a queen like bees, almost never gets cancer, and barely ages.

name: Malayan tapir
fact: Its black-and-white body breaks up its outline in moonlit jungle.

name: Greater roadrunner
fact: Can kill and eat rattlesnakes - it grabs them by the tail and whips their heads on rocks.

name: Kea
blurb: Species of bird endemic to New Zealand
fact: The world's only alpine parrot - famous for pulling the rubber off car windscreens.

name: Scotoplanes
blurb: Genus of deep-sea sea cucumbers known as sea pigs
fact: A deep-sea cucumber that walks on puffy water-filled legs, in herds.

name: Christmas Island red crab
fact: Each year tens of millions march to the sea at once, with crab bridges built over the roads.

name: Bombardier beetle
fact: Mixes chemicals in its abdomen to blast a boiling, popping spray at attackers.

name: Glasswing butterfly
fact: Its glassy wings are almost invisible in flight - the glasswing butterfly.

name: Sword-billed hummingbird
blurb: Species of bird from South America
fact: The only bird with a bill longer than its body - it has to groom with its feet.
credit: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK · CC BY 2.0

name: Banded archerfish
fact: Knocks insects off leaves with a jet of water spat from below the surface.

name: Ocellaris clownfish
fact: All clownfish are born male - when the group's female dies, the top male becomes her.

name: White-spotted pufferfish
fact: Males spend a week sculpting 2-metre circles in the sand with their fins to court females.
credit: Hiroshi Kawase, Yuki Kitajima, Daisuke Iwai · CC BY 4.0

name: Atlantic hagfish
fact: Can turn a bucket of seawater into slime in seconds - and ties itself in knots to clean off.

name: Pygmy marmoset
fact: The smallest monkey in the world - it gnaws holes in trees to drink the sap.

name: Philippine tarsier
fact: Each eyeball is bigger than its brain - and its eyes can't move, so it turns its head.

name: Mata mata
fact: Lies still on the river bed and sucks fish into its mouth like a vacuum cleaner.

name: Common basilisk
fact: Runs across the surface of water on its hind legs before sinking.

name: Frilled lizard
fact: Flares a huge frill, hisses - and if that fails, sprints away upright on its hind legs.
credit: Matt from Melbourne, Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Wallace's flying frog
fact: Glides between trees using its giant webbed feet as parachutes.

name: Surinam toad
fact: The eggs sink into the skin of the mother's back, and fully formed toadlets pop out of it.

name: Chambered nautilus
fact: A living fossil that floats by adjusting gas in the chambers of its shell.

name: Alvinella pompejana
fact: One of the most heat-tolerant complex animals - its tail sits in near-boiling vent water.
credit: National Science Foundation (University of Delaware College of Marine Studies) · Public domain

name: Atlantic horseshoe crab
fact: Its blue blood is used to test medicines and vaccines for bacteria.

name: Aardvark
fact: First in the dictionary - and can dig a burrow faster than a team of men with spades.

name: Southern cassowary
fact: Often called the most dangerous bird - its inner toe carries a 12 cm dagger-like claw.

name: Coconut crab
fact: The largest land invertebrate - its pinch is one of the strongest of any animal.

name: Hercules beetle
fact: One of the longest beetles in the world - males wrestle with their huge pincer-like horns.

name: Bullet ant
fact: Its sting tops the Schmidt pain index - it feels like being shot.

name: Electric eel
blurb: Genus of fishes in South America
fact: Not a true eel - it's a knifefish that can leap out of the water to shock threats.

name: Wilson's bird-of-paradise
fact: Its bare blue skull looks like a bright cap - and the male clears a dance floor in the forest.

name: Snowy albatross
fact: Has the longest wingspan of any living bird and can glide for hours without flapping.

name: Andean condor
fact: One condor flew over 170 km without flapping its wings once.

name: Giant armadillo
fact: Has the largest claw of any living animal for its size.

name: Gaur
blurb: Largest species of the bovid family
fact: The largest wild cattle in the world - even tigers usually avoid adults.

name: Bighorn sheep
blurb: Species of sheep native to North America
fact: Rams smash heads at over 30 km/h - a double-layered skull absorbs the blow.

name: Reef stonefish
fact: The world's most venomous fish - it looks exactly like a lumpy rock.

name: Giant moray
fact: Has a second set of jaws in its throat that shoot forward to drag prey down.

name: Atlantic bluefin tuna
fact: Keeps its body warmer than the sea around it - and crosses the Atlantic.

name: Giant oarfish
fact: The longest bony fish in the world - likely the source of many sea serpent tales.

name: Ascarosepion pfefferi
fact: Ripples with flashing purple and yellow and walks along the seabed instead of swimming.

name: Bobbit worm
fact: Hides in the sand with only its jaws showing, then snaps up passing fish.

name: Wandering glider dragonfly
fact: A dragonfly that migrates across oceans - the longest-distance flyer of any insect.
credit: Jeevan Jose, Kerala, India · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Pronghorn
blurb: Species of North American hoofed mammal
fact: The fastest land animal in the Americas - probably evolved to outrun the extinct American cheetah.

name: White-throated needletail
fact: Possibly the fastest bird in flapping flight - it rarely lands except to nest.

name: Eastern hognose snake
fact: If you flip it right side up while it's 'dead', it rolls straight back over.

name: Eastern gray squirrel
blurb: Species of squirrel native to North America
fact: Fakes burying nuts when it thinks it's being watched, to fool would-be thieves.

name: Common bottlenose dolphin
fact: Each dolphin has a signature whistle that works as its name.

name: Fossa
blurb: Cat-like species of mammal from Madagascar
fact: Looks like a cat but is closer to mongooses; its ankles rotate so it can run down trees head first.

name: Sunda pangolin
blurb: Species of pangolin found in southeast Asia
fact: Rolls into an armoured ball that even lions struggle to open.

name: Capybara
fact: The world's largest rodent, famously calm - other animals often sit on it.

name: Southern sea otter
fact: Floats on its back holding hands with other otters so nobody drifts off while asleep.
credit: Marshal Hedin from San Diego · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Kākāpō
fact: A flightless, nocturnal parrot that smells of honey - every single one has a name.

name: Northern glass frog
fact: While it sleeps it hides almost all its red blood cells in its liver, turning nearly invisible.

name: Spix's macaw
blurb: Species of macaw that is extinct in the wild
fact: Declared extinct in the wild in 2019, then released back into Brazil in 2022.
credit: Rüdiger Stehn from Kiel, Deutschland · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Okapi
fact: Looks like a zebra but is the giraffe's only living relative - and licks its own ears clean.

name: Aye-aye
fact: Taps on bark and listens for hollow grub tunnels, like an echo-locating woodpecker.

name: Chinese giant salamander
fact: The largest amphibian in the world - and it can bark like a baby.

name: Star-nosed mole
fact: The fastest eater known - it can find and eat a morsel in under a quarter of a second.

name: Hoatzin
blurb: Species of bird in South America
fact: Ferments leaves in its gut like a cow, giving it a smell like manure.

name: Leatherback sea turtle
fact: The largest turtle alive, with a rubbery shell instead of a hard one, and it lives mostly on jellyfish.
credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Southeast Region · Public domain

name: Sumatran rhinoceros
fact: The hairy rhino - the closest living relative of the extinct woolly rhinoceros.

name: Blue whale
blurb: Species of whale; largest animal known
fact: The largest animal that has ever lived - bigger than any dinosaur.

name: Water bear (tardigrade)
fact: A 'water bear' that survived a trip to open space in 2007.
credit: Schokraie E, Warnken U, Hotz-Wagenblatt A, Grohme MA, Hengherr S, et al. (2012) · CC BY 2.5

name: Mimic octopus
fact: Impersonates lionfish, sea snakes and flatfish, picking whichever scares off the current threat.

name: Blue dragon sea slug
fact: The 'blue dragon' eats Portuguese man o' war and stores their stinging cells to use itself.
credit: Taro Taylor from Sydney, Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Platypus
fact: A venomous, egg-laying mammal with a duck bill - and it glows blue-green under UV light.

name: Indo-Pacific sailfish
fact: Hunts in packs, raising its sail to herd sardines and slashing through them with its bill.

name: Hyacinth macaw
fact: The largest flying parrot in the world.

name: Japanese spider crab
fact: Has the longest legs of any arthropod.

name: Highland cattle
fact: Its long fringe (a 'dossan') keeps flies and rain out of its eyes.

name: Corn snake
fact: Named after the pattern on its belly, which looks like kernels of Indian corn.

name: Striped skunk
fact: Stamps its feet and fakes charges first - it would rather not waste its spray.

name: Maine Coon
fact: One of the biggest domestic cats - one held the record for longest cat at 123 cm.

name: Shiba Inu
fact: The dog behind the 'Doge' meme - it lets out a dramatic scream when it doesn't get its way.
credit: Takashiba at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Border Collie
fact: A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of over a thousand toys.

name: Cockatiel
fact: Learns whistled tunes more readily than words - its crest flattens or rises with its mood.
credit: Photo by: Ganatron – paulweberphoto.com · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: European praying mantis
fact: Has a single ear in the middle of its chest, tuned to hear hunting bats.

name: Common raccoon dog
fact: The only dog-family animal that hibernates - and it can climb trees.

name: Common raven
blurb: Large, black species of passerine bird
fact: Plays games like sliding down snowy roofs on its back - just for fun.

name: Ring-tailed lemur
fact: Males rub their tails with scent from their wrists and wave them at rivals in stink fights.

name: Sunda slow loris
blurb: Species of primate found in South East Asia
fact: One of the only venomous primates - it licks a gland in its elbow to make a toxic bite.
credit: David Haring / Duke Lemur Center · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Brown-throated sloth
fact: Climbs down once a week to poop, and its fur is home to algae and moths.

name: Meerkat
blurb: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa
fact: Teaches its young to eat scorpions by bringing them dead ones, then disarmed ones, then live ones.

name: Proboscis monkey
fact: The male's huge drooping nose amplifies its honking calls - and impresses females.

name: Japanese macaque
fact: The world's most northerly non-human primate - some troops bathe in hot springs in winter.

name: Mandrill
blurb: Species of Old World monkey from Africa
fact: The largest monkey - mandrills gather in the biggest primate groups ever recorded.

name: Gelada
fact: The only primate that lives mostly on grass - herds of hundreds graze on cliff tops.

name: Golden snub-nosed monkey
fact: Its flat, upturned nose may help it avoid frostbite in the snowy mountains of China.

name: Binturong
blurb: Asian mammal also known as a bearcat
fact: Smells exactly like buttered popcorn - from the same chemical in its urine.

name: Kirk's dik-dik
fact: Named after its whistling alarm call - and mates for life.

name: Ocean sunfish
fact: The heaviest bony fish - it looks like a giant swimming head with fins.
credit: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration · Public domain

name: Orchid mantis
fact: Looks so much like an orchid that insects fly straight to it - more than to real flowers.

name: Walrus
blurb: Species of marine mammal with tusks
fact: Uses its tusks to haul itself out of the water onto the ice.

name: West Indian manatee
fact: Its closest living relatives are elephants - and sailors once mistook it for mermaids.

name: Dugong
fact: The only strictly plant-eating marine mammal - it grazes seagrass meadows like a sea cow.

name: Beluga whale
fact: Chirps, whistles and clicks so much sailors called it the sea canary.
credit: Javier Yaya Tur / CIUDAD DE LAS ARTES Y LAS CIENCIAS from Valencia, España · CC BY 2.0

name: Emperor tamarin
fact: Named as a joke for its likeness to the moustached German emperor.

name: Honduran white bat
blurb: Species of bat that constructs tents
fact: Snips leaves so they fold into tents, where little huddles of white bats sleep.

name: Texas horned lizard
fact: Squirts blood from its eyes at coyotes and dogs - the blood tastes foul to them.
credit: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM · CC0

name: Argentine horned frog
fact: Its mouth is so big it tries to eat things nearly its own size - sometimes fatally.
credit: Melanie Mae Bryan from Greensboro, NC, USA · CC BY 2.0

name: Muskox
fact: Herds form a circle with horns facing out and the calves in the middle.

name: Red lionfish
fact: Invaded the Atlantic and Caribbean - people are now encouraged to catch and eat it.
credit: Photo by Jens Petersen, Edited by User:Olegiwit (cloned in part of fins) and Fir · CC BY 2.5

name: Margay
fact: Can turn its ankles round to run head-first down a tree trunk like a squirrel.

name: Iguanodon
fact: Its thumb spike was first put on its nose - one of the earliest dinosaurs ever named.

name: Yutyrannus
fact: A giant tyrannosaur relative covered in fluffy feathers - the largest feathered animal known.
credit: Laika ac from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Borealopelta
fact: So well preserved it's called a dinosaur mummy - even its last meal of ferns survived.

stats.label: Preserved
stats.value: Like a statue - skin and armour

credit: Nobu Tamura email:nobu.tamura@yahoo.com http://spinops.blogspot.com/ · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Markhor
fact: Its name may mean "snake-eater" - its corkscrew horns are some of the most spectacular of any goat.

name: Northern giant hornet
blurb: Predatory hornet, largest in the world
fact: A small group can wipe out an entire honey-bee hive in a few hours.

name: Frilled shark
fact: A living fossil with the longest known pregnancy of any vertebrate.
credit: This illustration was made by Citron You must credit this : Citron / CC-BY-SA-3. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Alligator snapping turtle
fact: Lies still with its mouth open, wiggling a pink worm-like lure on its tongue to catch fish.
credit: Gary M. Stolz/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service · Public domain

name: Bearded vulture
fact: Eats bones - and drops big ones from great heights onto rocks to crack them open.

name: Blakiston's fish owl
fact: The world's largest owl species - it wades in icy rivers to catch fish.

name: Common vampire bat
blurb: Species of bat native to the Americas
fact: Shares blood meals with roostmates who went hungry - and remembers who helped it.

name: Dhole
fact: A whistling wild dog whose packs can drive off tigers.

name: Giant anteater
fact: Flicks its tongue 150 times a minute and eats up to 30,000 ants and termites a day.

name: African buffalo
fact: Herds vote on where to go next by standing up and facing their chosen direction.

name: Southern elephant seal
fact: The largest seal - males roar through an inflatable trunk-like nose.

name: Moose
fact: Can dive nearly 6 metres to eat water plants - and swims for kilometres.

name: Deinonychus
fact: Its discovery convinced scientists dinosaurs were fast and active, and related to birds.

name: Deinocheirus
fact: Known only from giant arms for 50 years - the rest turned out to have a hump and a duck bill.

name: Inland taipan
blurb: Extremely venomous snake native to Australia
fact: Has the most toxic venom of any snake - but is so shy that bites are almost unknown.

name: Hippopotamus
fact: Among Africa's most dangerous animals - and it secretes a red, sunscreen-like 'blood sweat'.

name: Swordfish
blurb: Fish which has a long, pointed bill
fact: Has special organs that heat its eyes and brain for hunting in cold, deep water.

name: Steller's sea eagle
blurb: Bird of prey species native to East Asia
fact: One of the heaviest eagles in the world, with a giant golden-orange beak.

name: Gyrfalcon
fact: The largest falcon - in medieval falconry, only kings could fly one.
credit: Falco_rusticolus_white.jpg: Ólafur Larsen derivative work: Bogbumper (talk) · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Leopard seal
fact: The only seal that regularly hunts other warm-blooded animals - it has a reptile-like grin.

name: Golden eagle
fact: Has been known to take down deer - one of the most widespread and powerful eagles.

name: Black marlin
fact: One of the fastest fish in the ocean - its pectoral fins are rigid and can't be folded.
credit: Queensland State Archives from Runcorn, Queensland, Australia · Public domain

name: Australian box jellyfish
fact: One of the most venomous animals on Earth - and it has 24 eyes.
credit: Avispa marina.jpg: Guido Gautsch, Toyota, Japan derivative work: Mithril (talk) · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Raccoon
blurb: Medium-sized mammal native to North America
fact: About two-thirds of the touch-sensing part of its brain is devoted to its paws.

name: Sierra Nevada red fox
fact: Rediscovered near Sonora Pass in 2010 after decades without a confirmed sighting.

name: Carniolan honey bee
fact: Tells hive-mates where flowers are with a 'waggle dance' that encodes direction and distance.
credit: Richard Bartz, Munich Makro Freak & Beemaster Hubert Seibring, Munich which gave · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: Red-eyed tree frog
fact: Embryos can sense a snake shaking their egg clutch and hatch on the spot to escape.
credit: Red-eyed Tree Frog (Agalychnis callidryas) 3.jpg: Geoff Gallice from Gainesville · CC BY 2.0

name: Koala
blurb: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia
fact: Has fingerprints so close to ours they could confuse a crime scene.

name: Giant Pacific octopus
fact: Has blue blood and can taste with its suckers.

name: Fennec fox
fact: The smallest canid - its giant ears dump heat and hear prey moving underground.

name: Virginia opossum
fact: 'Playing possum' is involuntary: it faints, drools and smells like death for up to hours.

stats.label: Teeth
stats.value: 50 - most of any N. American land mammal

name: American alligator
blurb: Crocodilian native to the Southeastern United States
fact: Has been around, nearly unchanged, for about 8 million years.

name: Axolotl
fact: Stays a larva its whole life, keeping its feathery gills forever.

name: Golden poison frog
fact: Its poison comes from its diet - captive-bred frogs fed crickets are harmless.

name: Satanic leaf-tailed gecko
blurb: Species of gecko endemic to Madagascar
fact: Looks so much like a dead leaf that it even has fake bite marks and decay on its tail.

name: Mandarinfish
fact: One of only two vertebrates known to make true blue pigment.

name: Philippine eagle
blurb: Endangered species of eagle in the Philippines
fact: Once called the 'monkey-eating eagle'; harming one in the Philippines can mean 12 years in jail.

name: Goblin shark
fact: Its jaws shoot forward like a slingshot to snatch prey.

name: Secretarybird
fact: Kills snakes by stomping them, with kicks faster than a blink.

name: Northern white rhinoceros
fact: Only two remain, Najin and Fatu, guarded around the clock in Kenya.

name: Amazon river dolphin
fact: Its unfused neck bones let it weave through flooded forests.

name: Giant squid
blurb: Deep-ocean dwelling squid in the family Architeuthidae
fact: Has the largest eyes of any animal (tied with the colossal squid).
credit: Natural History Museum of Denmark · CC BY 4.0

name: Sperm whale
fact: Makes the loudest sound of any animal.

name: King cobra
blurb: Group of venomous snakes from Asia
fact: The longest venomous snake - it hunts other snakes, cobras included.
credit: Michael Allen Smith from Seattle, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Bowhead whale
blurb: Baleen whale endemic to the Arctic
fact: The longest-lived mammal - one was found with a 19th-century harpoon point in it.
credit: Vicki Beaver, Alaska Fisheries Science Center, NOAA FIsheries, Marine Mammal Per · Public domain

name: Peregrine falcon
blurb: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey
fact: The fastest animal on Earth - in a hunting dive it moves faster than a Formula 1 car.

name: Peacock mantis shrimp
fact: Punches so fast the water boils into flashes of light, and it can break aquarium glass.

name: Thorny devil
fact: Drinks through its skin: grooves between its scales wick water to its mouth.

name: Leafy seadragon
fact: Disguised as floating seaweed - and, like seahorses, the males carry the eggs.

name: Bee hummingbird
fact: The smallest bird in the world - its nest is the size of a coin.

name: Giant golden-crowned flying fox
fact: One of the biggest bats in the world - and it only eats fruit.

name: Paradise flying snake
fact: Launches from trees, flattens its body and slithers through the air to glide.
credit: Alan Couch from Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Sun bear
fact: Uses its huge tongue to slurp honey and insects out of tree holes.

name: Serval
fact: Leaps straight up to swat birds out of the air - one of the most successful cat hunters.

name: Pallas's cat
fact: Has the densest fur of any cat and an expression of permanent disappointment.
credit: Sander van der Wel · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Spectacled bear
fact: The only bear in South America - Paddington Bear came from "darkest Peru".

name: Pachycephalosaurus
fact: Its domed skull was up to 25 cm of solid bone - debate continues over whether it head-butted.

name: Humpback whale
fact: Males sing complex songs that spread from population to population like hit records.

name: Gaboon viper
fact: Has the longest fangs of any snake and the highest venom yield.

name: Reticulated python
fact: The longest snake in the world - it has turned up on remote islands after swimming.
credit: This photography was created by Mariluna. Other photos see here. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Maned wolf
fact: Looks like a fox on stilts - it isn't a wolf or a fox, and half its diet is fruit.

name: African wild dog
fact: Packs decide whether to go hunting by sneezing - enough sneezes and they go.

name: Bonobo
fact: Settles arguments through affection rather than fighting - and females run the group.

name: Bornean orangutan
fact: Builds a fresh nest in the trees every night - and sometimes uses a leaf as an umbrella.

name: Black-footed cat
blurb: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa
fact: One of Africa's smallest cats - and the most successful hunter of all cats.
credit: Patrick Ch. Apfeld, derivative editing by Poke2001 · CC BY 3.0

name: Portuguese man o' war
fact: Not a single animal but a colony of specialised individuals sailing together.
credit: Image courtesy of Islands in the Sea 2002, NOAA/OER. · Public domain

name: Vampire squid
fact: Neither a vampire nor a squid - it eats drifting debris and turns its cloak inside out when threatened.

name: Siberian musk deer
fact: Males have long fangs instead of antlers and use them to fight rivals.

name: Chimpanzee
fact: Some chimps make spears to hunt bushbabies - and crack nuts with stone hammers.

name: Stegosaurus stenops
blurb: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur
fact: Its tail spikes are officially nicknamed the 'thagomizer', after a Far Side cartoon.

name: Velociraptor mongoliensis
fact: The real one was turkey-sized and feathered - Jurassic Park's were based on Deinonychus.

name: Allosaurus
fact: May have attacked by slamming its open upper jaw down like a hatchet.

name: Carnotaurus
blurb: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period
fact: Its name means 'meat-eating bull' - with bull horns and almost useless stub arms.
credit: Lida Xing and Yi Liu · CC BY 2.5

name: Mamenchisaurus
blurb: Sauropod dinosaur genus from Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous Period
fact: Its neck made up nearly half of its body length - one of the longest necks of any animal.
credit: The original uploader was ДиБгд at Russian Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Black mamba
fact: One of the fastest snakes - named for the inky-black inside of its mouth, not its skin.

name: Green anaconda
fact: The heaviest snake in the world - it spends most of its time in water.

name: Colossal squid
fact: The heaviest invertebrate - with the biggest eyes of any known animal.
credit: This illustration was made by Citron You must credit this : Citron / CC-BY-SA-3. · CC BY 3.0

name: Tiger shark
fact: Called the "garbage can of the sea" - license plates and tyres have turned up in its stomach.

name: Whale shark
fact: The largest fish in the sea - every one has its own pattern of spots, like a fingerprint.

name: Nile crocodile
fact: A fearsome predator that gently carries its newly hatched babies in its jaws.

name: Spotted hyena
fact: Not a scavenger at heart - it kills most of its food and its laugh is a social signal.

name: Crowned eagle
fact: Africa's most powerful eagle - it takes monkeys and small antelope from the treetops.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Brachiosaurus
blurb: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period
fact: Stood like a giraffe, with longer front legs - its head reached a four-storey window.

name: Utahraptor
blurb: Genus of dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous
fact: The biggest raptor - a polar-bear-sized hunter with a 24 cm sickle claw.

name: Therizinosaurus
blurb: Dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous period
fact: Had the longest claws of any known animal - and probably used them to strip leaves.

name: Greenland shark
fact: The longest-lived vertebrate known - some alive today were born before the U.S. existed.

name: Harpy eagle
fact: Its talons are longer than a grizzly bear's claws.

name: Komodo dragon
fact: Females can reproduce without a male - virgin births have happened in zoos.

name: Honey badger
fact: Its loose skin lets it twist round and bite back while held - it eats venomous snakes.

name: Ankylosaurus
blurb: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period
fact: Basically a living tank - its tail club could smash the leg bones of a predator.

name: Argentinosaurus
blurb: Extinct genus of giant sauropod dinosaur
fact: One of the heaviest land animals ever - a single vertebra is taller than a person.

stats.label: Record
stats.value: Among the biggest land animals ever

name: Emperor penguin
blurb: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica
fact: Fathers balance the egg on their feet through two months of Antarctic winter without eating.
credit: Ian Duffy from UK · CC BY 2.0

name: Snowy owl
fact: Hunts in daylight - in the Arctic summer there's no night to hunt in.

name: Great horned owl
fact: One of the few animals that regularly eats skunks - it has a poor sense of smell.

name: Himalayan red panda
fact: Was named a 'panda' about 50 years before the giant panda.

name: Mountain gorilla
fact: Population has been slowly rising thanks to conservation - a rare comeback story.

name: Great hammerhead
fact: Uses its hammer like a metal detector, sweeping the sand for buried stingrays.

name: Wolverine
fact: Pound for pound one of the toughest animals alive - it drives bears and wolves off their kills.

name: Spirit bear
blurb: Subspecies of the American black bear
fact: A black bear born white - up to 1 in 10 on some British Columbia islands.
credit: Maximilian Helm from Dresden, Deutschland · CC BY 2.0

name: Saltwater crocodile
fact: The largest living reptile, with the strongest bite ever measured in a living animal.
credit: Obtained from Molly Ebersold of the St. Augustine Alligator Farm · Public domain

name: Kodiak bear
blurb: Largest subspecies of brown bears/grizzly bears
fact: The biggest brown bear on Earth - and it lives only on Alaska's Kodiak islands.

name: African bush elephant
fact: The largest land animal - it picks up rumbles from kilometres away through the soles of its feet.

name: Red kangaroo
fact: The largest marsupial - it can clear 8 metres in a single bound.
credit: fir0002 flagstaffotos [at] gmail.com Canon 20D + Canon 70-200mm f/2.8 L · GFDL 1.2

name: Canada lynx
fact: Its population rises and falls in a 10-year cycle with the snowshoe hares it eats.

name: Gharial
blurb: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent
fact: Males grow a bulb on their snout called a ghara, after an Indian pot - it buzzes their calls.

name: Caracal
fact: Leaps into the air and swats birds out of the sky - sometimes several at once.

name: Bull shark
fact: Can live in fresh water and has been found thousands of kilometres up the Amazon.

name: Cougar
blurb: Wild cat species native to the Americas
fact: Holds the record for the most names of any animal - puma, mountain lion, panther and more.

name: Grizzly bear
fact: Can smell food from kilometres away and outrun a racehorse over a short sprint.

name: Triceratops horridus
fact: Had one of the largest skulls of any land animal - and fought T. rex, judging by bite marks.
credit: Source: Allie_Caulfield Derivative: User:MathKnight · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Giganotosaurus
blurb: Carcharodontosaurid dinosaur genus from the Cretaceous period
fact: One of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs - longer than T. rex, but with a lighter skull.

name: Clouded leopard
fact: Its fangs are, for its size, as long as a sabre-toothed cat's - and it can hang from branches by its hind feet.

stats.label: Canines
stats.value: Longest for its size of any cat

credit: Spencer Wright from North Walsham, England · CC BY 2.0

name: Arctic fox
fact: Hears lemmings under the snow, then dives headfirst through it to catch them.

name: Greater blue-ringed octopus
fact: One of the most venomous animals in the sea, yet it fits in your palm.

name: Siberian (Amur) tiger
fact: The biggest wild cat on Earth.

name: Orca
fact: The ocean's apex predator - pods hunt great white sharks, and the sharks abandon the area for months.

name: Great white shark
fact: Launches its whole body out of the water to ambush seals from below.
credit: Pterantula (Terry Goss) at en.wikipedia · CC BY 2.5

name: Polar bear
blurb: Species of bear native to the Arctic
fact: The largest land carnivore - its fur is actually see-through and its skin is black.

name: Asiatic cheetah
fact: The last Asiatic cheetahs survive only in the deserts of central Iran.

name: Snow leopard
fact: Can't roar - and wraps its huge tail around its face like a scarf.

name: Jaguar
blurb: Large cat native to the Americas
fact: Kills with a single bite straight through the skull - and stalks caimans in rivers.

name: Bengal tiger
blurb: Tiger population on the Indian subcontinent
fact: Its stripes are on its skin as well as its fur - every tiger's pattern is unique.

name: Black panther
fact: Not a species of its own - a black leopard or jaguar whose spots still show in bright light.

name: Shortfin mako shark
fact: The fastest shark in the sea - it can launch itself many metres out of the water.

name: Amur leopard
fact: One of the rarest big cats on Earth, surviving in snowy forests of Russia and China.

name: Asiatic lion
fact: Once ranged from Greece to India - now lives wild in a single forest in Gujarat.

name: Bald eagle
blurb: Bird of prey species of North America
fact: Builds the largest nests of any North American bird - one weighed nearly 3 tonnes.
credit: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK · CC BY 2.0

name: Arctic wolf
fact: Lives in total darkness for months each winter and can go weeks without eating.

name: Tyrannosaurus rex
fact: Had the strongest bite of any land animal ever - strong enough to crush bone.

name: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
fact: The longest meat-eating dinosaur known - and it hunted in rivers, with a paddle-like tail.
